body:
#### References to other Issues or PRs

- Partially fixes #21618 by evaluating `sin` and `cos` on `SetExpr` intervals with concrete endpoints.
- Incorporates the approach proposed in #29682, with an improvement to preserve handling of `EmptySet`; closes #29682
- Partially fixes #29675 by preventing enumeration of infinitely many singularities. The efficiency of processing large finite sets of singularities remains unresolved.

#### Brief description of what is fixed or changed

Improves evaluation of the image of a function over an interval:

- Restricts critical-point solving to the given interval, allowing functions such as `sin` and `cos` to be evaluated when they have infinitely many critical points globally but finitely many within the interval.
- Corrects endpoint openness by determining whether an extremal value is attained within the domain.
- Allows `sin` and `cos` applied to a `SetExpr` interval to return an evaluated interval when possible.
- Checks whether the set of singularities is finite before attempting enumeration. Infinite or unresolved sets are left unevaluated, while `EmptySet` and finite singularity sets continue to be handled normally.

#### Other comments

The singularity-handling change is based on the approach proposed by @SarvaarthN in #29682.

A possible future improvement is to handle equally spaced singularities symbolically, avoiding enumeration even when there are many finitely many points.

#### AI Generation Disclosure

Collaboration with ChatGPT who wrote this OP after a minimal description.

#### Release Notes

<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
* sets
  * Improved evaluation of `sin` and `cos` on `SetExpr` intervals.
  * Corrected endpoint inclusion in interval image calculations.
  * Prevented enumeration of infinite singularity sets in `imageset`.
<!-- END RELEASE NOTES -->

commits.message:
Avoid enumerating infinite imageset singularities

Adapt the guard proposed by Sarvaarth Narang in sympy/sympy#29682,
while preserving evaluation for EmptySet singularities.

See sympy/sympy#29675.

+def test_imageset_interval_critical_points():
+    # Solve only for critical points in the interval, not on all of C.
+    assert imageset(Lambda(x, sin(x)), Interval(1, 2)) == \
+        Interval(sin(1), 1)
+    assert imageset(Lambda(x, cos(x)), Interval(1, 2)) == \
+        Interval(cos(2), cos(1))
+    assert imageset(sin, Interval(0, 2*pi)) == Interval(-1, 1)
+    assert imageset(Lambda(x, sin(x)), Interval(-2, 1)) == \
+        Interval(-1, sin(1))
+

+def test_imageset_interval_open_extrema():
+    # The limit at an excluded endpoint need not be in the image.
+    f = Lambda(x, 2 - (x - 1)**2)

+        Interval.open(1, 4)

+        Interval.Ropen(0, 1)
+    # A value reached at the other, included endpoint must remain included.

+        Interval(0, 1)
+    assert imageset(Lambda(x, sin(x)), Interval.Lopen(0, pi)) == \
+        Interval(0, 1)
+    assert imageset(Lambda(x, sin(x)), Interval.open(0, pi)) == \
+        Interval.Lopen(0, 1)

linked.author: smichr
linked.body:
from #14251, when SetExpr is the argument of a function it is handled less gracefully than when the argument is AccumBounds:
```python
>>> cos(AccumBounds(-1, 2))
AccumBounds(cos(2), 1)
>>> cos(SetExpr(Interval(-1, 2)))
SetExpr(ImageSet(Lambda(x, cos(x)), Interval(-1, 2)))
>>> var('a b', real=True)
>>> sin(AccumBounds(a, b))
TypeError: input failed to evaluate
>>> sin(SetExpr(Interval(a, b)))
SetExpr(ImageSet(Lambda(x, sin(x)), Interval(a, b)))
```
linked.title: function(SetExpr(...)) could be handled better

linked.author: JosephMehdiyev
linked.body:
This will try to evaluate for a long time (possibly infinite)
```Python
x = Symbol("x", real=True)
imageset(x,tan(x),  S.Reals)
```
seems like `imageset` tries to calculate every singularity individually?
`imageset(x,tan(x), Interval(-100,100))` lists every singularity individually. Am I using `imageset` wrong?
Similar thing happens with `cot(x)`. I would expect a proper answer from this, but at least there should be some safehandling to avoid infinite calculations like this

There is a `TODO` comment on `sympy/sets/handlers/functions.py` about this
linked.title: `imageset` on `tan(x)`  takes  long time
